name: Abnormal AI
hq: San Francisco, CA, USA (2024 releases datelined San Francisco; 2025 rebrand release datelined Las Vegas)
business_model: SaaS behavioral-AI security platform, led by email security and expanding to collaboration and cloud applications, sold to enterprises on subscription.
overview: Abnormal AI sells AI-native 'human behavior security', starting with cloud email protection. In August 2024 it reported more than $200M ARR, 100%+ year-over-year ARR growth and 2,400+ customer organizations including 17% of the Fortune 500. In April 2025 it rebranded from Abnormal Security to Abnormal AI to signal expansion beyond email into a broader behavioral AI platform. Its engineering blog describes a real-time detection engine fed by Kafka and Redis peaking at 35,000 QPS plus a Spark batch system processing about 3 TB/day.

sources.title: Software Engineer I, Data Platform (Abnormal AI)
sources.excerpt: Data Platform team runs storage (PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, Redis, RocksDB, DynamoDB), batch and stream processing (Kafka, Spark), orchestration (Airflow, DBT) on AWS with Databricks; listing removed 2026-08-06.

sources.title: Abnormal AI Innovation: High-Scale Aggregation Systems in Production
sources.excerpt: Signals DAG runs in a realtime scorer, a realtime aggregation system (Kafka, Go consumers, Redis; peaks ~35k QPS) and a Spark/Airflow batch job (~3 TB/day). Parallel batch and realtime paths created a leaky abstraction; team plans a Lambda-architecture unification.

sources.title: Abnormal AI Innovation: Inside the Fault-Tolerant Scoring Engine
sources.excerpt: Real-time detection engine depends on many upstream signals (an employee database, Whois, historical sender stats); FTS framework keeps scoring on healthy signals and rescores after recovery. Growing dependency webs caused firefighting.

sources.title: How Abnormal Taught AI Agents To Write Detectors
sources.excerpt: AI Detection Agents (deep research + adaptive detection) turn customer-reported misses into deployed detectors, evaluated against historical traffic with LLM labeling; context is thousands of attack patterns and millions of mailboxes. No data stores named.

sources.title: Abnormal Security Series D at $5.1B valuation

buying_signals.title: Separate realtime and batch aggregation paths flagged as a leaky abstraction
buying_signals.detail: Engineering blog says building realtime (Kafka/Redis) and batch (Spark) aggregation systems in parallel forces ML engineers to account for differences, the batch system had to be redesigned for load, and the team plans to unify them under a Lambda architecture. A single engine serving streaming ingest plus analytical aggregation is a relevant conversation, though the team's chosen direction is Lambda, not consolidation.

verified_facts.fact: Realtime aggregation peaks at about 35,000 QPS using Kafka, Go and Redis; batch job processes about 3 TB/day on Spark with Airflow.
Engineering describes the parallel batch/realtime systems as a leaky abstraction and plans to unify them under a Lambda architecture.
Data Platform team operates PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, Redis, RocksDB, DynamoDB, Kafka, Spark, Airflow, DBT on AWS and uses Databricks.
August 2024: $250M Series D at $5.1B valuation, ARR over $200M growing 100%+ YoY, 2,400+ customer organizations.
Renamed from Abnormal Security to Abnormal AI in April 2025, positioning beyond email security.
In 2026 the company built AI agents that generate and test detectors from customer-reported misses.

inferences.inference: Keeping separate realtime (Redis) and batch (Spark) code paths in sync is an ongoing engineering cost, making a single real-time analytics engine worth discussing.
Expansion beyond email will add new event sources and volume to the detection pipeline.
Redis holding aggregates is likely memory-cost sensitive at growing scale, but no source states cost pressure.

What do the detection agents query when they evaluate a candidate detector against historical traffic, and how long does that take?
Which workloads run on OpenSearch today, and is vector search part of the roadmap?
opportunity_hypothesis: Hypothesis to validate: Abnormal's detection pipeline maintains parallel Kafka/Redis realtime and Spark batch aggregation paths that engineering itself calls a leaky abstraction, and it plans to re-architect them. SingleStore could serve streaming ingest, real-time aggregates and historical backfills from one engine, simplifying that unification. Fit depends on whether the Lambda redesign is already committed and on Redis/Spark cost.

outreach.subject: Your realtime + batch aggregation unification
outreach.body: Hi - I read Fang Deng's July 2025 post on the Signals DAG: realtime aggregation at ~35k QPS on Kafka and Redis, a Spark batch job at ~3 TB/day, and a plan to unify the two under a Lambda architecture. Some teams in that position test whether one engine can ingest from Kafka and serve both live aggregates and historical backfills with SQL, so there is one code path to keep consistent. SingleStore does that, and adds vector and full-text search. Would a 20-minute comparison against your unification options be useful? If the design is already settled, I'd still like to hear what drove it.
